content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 20, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Multidisciplinary Care Resolves Severe Disseminated Tuberculosis and Hepatitis in Late Pregnancy by November 16, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Multidisciplinary Care Resolves Severe Disseminated Tuberculosis and Hepatitis in Late Pregnancy Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram In a published clinical report from Qinghai, medical specialists detailed the successful multidisciplinary management of a critically ill twenty-four-year-old pregnant pastoralist diagnosed with concurrent hematogenous disseminated tuberculosis, tuberculous meningitis, and active hepatitis B infection during her third trimester. The patient, a primigravida at thirty weeks of gestation with documented household exposure to pulmonary tuberculosis through her sister, initially presented after experiencing two weeks of intermittent headache and vomiting alongside worsening lower back pain. Given the substantial maternal and fetal risks associated with central nervous system mycobacterial dissemination and simultaneous active viral replication, a coordinated multidisciplinary team assembled to manage the compounded diagnostic and therapeutic challenges presented by this life-threatening triad in an understudied population. Physical and laboratory evaluations conducted upon initial presentation demonstrated marked systemic and neurological involvement. Her vital signs recorded a temperature of 38.0 degrees Celsius, heart rate of 90 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 25 breaths per minute, blood pressure of 125 over 75 millimeters of mercury, and oxygen saturation of 97 percent on supplemental nasal oxygen. Physical examination revealed nuchal rigidity, positive Kernig’s and Brudzinski’s signs, and right conjunctival injection without jaundice, rash, or lymphadenopathy. Diagnostic lumbar puncture demonstrated severe intracranial hypertension with an opening pressure exceeding 330 millimeters of water. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed a nucleated cell count of 130 times ten to the sixth per liter, elevated protein at 2.37 grams per liter, glucose decreased to 0.59 millimoles per liter, and marked chloride reduction. Trace Mycobacterium tuberculosis was detected via cerebrospinal fluid Xpert testing without rifampicin resistance, while chest computed tomography confirmed diffuse bilateral miliary nodules. Discover more Pregnancy pregnant Find Neurologists Concurrent laboratory investigations established active hepatitis B co-infection alongside physiological disturbances. Serological testing confirmed a triple-positive profile with positive hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis B e-antigen, and hepatitis B core antibody, accompanied by a hepatitis B virus DNA load of 1.94 times ten to the eighth international units per milliliter. Both the tuberculin skin test and interferon-gamma release assay yielded positive results, while testing for human immunodeficiency virus was negative. Arterial blood gas testing revealed a pH of 7.49, a partial pressure of carbon dioxide of 24 millimeters of mercury, a partial pressure of oxygen of 95 millimeters of mercury, sodium of 123 millimoles per liter, potassium of 3.2 millimoles per liter, calcium of 1.07 millimoles per liter, glucose of 7.4 millimoles per liter, and lactate of 1.4 millimoles per liter. Hematological testing indicated a white blood cell count of 8.05 times ten to the ninth per liter with 86.20 percent neutrophils, hemoglobin of 98 grams per liter, and procalcitonin of 0.08 nanograms per milliliter. Discover more Check Symptoms Read Med Journals pregnancy Track Pregnancy Upon transfer to the intensive care setting, the multidisciplinary team addressed the acute dilemma of managing severe intracranial hypertension in late pregnancy without compromising fetal safety. Conventional hyperosmolar agents, including mannitol and glycerol fructose, were intentionally withheld due to safety concerns regarding their classification as Pregnancy Category C substances. Instead, clinicians performed continuous lumbar cisternal cerebrospinal fluid drainage to directly control intracranial pressure. The initial anti-tuberculosis regimen initiated on October 10 consisted of oral isoniazid at 0.6 grams once daily, rifampicin at 0.45 grams once daily, and ethambutol at 0.75 grams once daily. Pyrazinamide was deliberately omitted from this first-line combination due to the patient’s severe gastrointestinal intolerance to oral medications. Intravenous furosemide was briefly administered at 20 milligrams every twelve hours to maintain fluid balance, but clinicians discontinued it after five days when ultrasound revealed diminished amniotic fluid volume, maintaining close monitoring to correct hyponatremia and hypokalemia. During the initial treatment phase, clinicians systematically managed several concurrent clinical complications that emerged alongside the primary mycobacterial infection. The patient developed recurrent fever peaking at 38.7 degrees Celsius, prompting microbiological investigations. Testing detected positive immunoglobulin M against Mycoplasma pneumoniae, and sputum cultures yielded Candida albicans. In response, medical staff administered oral azithromycin at 250 milligrams daily for five days and instituted topical nystatin mouthwash for oral candidiasis. Concurrently, endocrine screening identified a thyroid-stimulating hormone concentration of 5.022 milliunits per liter with normal free thyroxine, establishing subclinical hypothyroidism of pregnancy that normalized following daily administration of 25 micrograms of levothyroxine. On October 15, the patient experienced clinical deterioration marked by fever reaching 39.0 degrees Celsius, which the multidisciplinary team attributed to inadequate control of the central nervous system infection. In response, the treatment group escalated the antimicrobial strategy to include isoniazid at 0.6 grams daily, rifampicin at 0.45 grams daily, linezolid at 0.6 grams daily, and intravenous moxifloxacin at 250 milliliters daily. Ethambutol was withdrawn to eliminate the compounding risk of fetal retrobulbar optic neuritis associated with combined linezolid administration. To control active hepatitis B replication and mitigate potential hepatic injury from anti-tuberculosis medications, clinicians initiated tenofovir disoproxil fumarate at 0.3 grams daily following informed consent discussions. This intensified therapy adhered to World Health Organization guidance permitting linezolid-containing regimens under structured monitoring during pregnancy, ensuring high cerebrospinal fluid drug penetration while balancing risks of maternal marrow suppression. Repeat lumbar puncture demonstrated normalized intracranial pressure at 130 millimeters of water, confirming effective intracranial hypertension control under the revised therapeutic regimen. Serial ultrasound assessments indicated an amniotic fluid index of 71 millimeters and a maximum vertical pocket of 26 millimeters. At the family's request, a lower-segment cesarean delivery was performed on November 19, 2025, following multidisciplinary assessment that delivery after 34 weeks was appropriate to balance the risks of preterm birth against maternal tuberculosis control. The operation delivered a live preterm female infant in cephalic presentation weighing 2320 grams with a one-minute Apgar score of 8. The neonate received hepatitis B vaccination and immunoglobulin to prevent transmission before pediatric transfer, and both mother and infant were discharged without complications on December 1, 2025. Long-term post-discharge monitoring confirmed sustained clinical recovery for both mother and child. At a comprehensive follow-up examination conducted on July 30, 2026, seven months postpartum, maternal health remained stable with normal hepatic and renal biochemical indices and no clinical or laboratory evidence of mycobacterial relapse. The authors emphasized that pregnancy creates a distinct immunological state characterized by elevated circulating progesterone and estrogen levels. These hormonal changes selectively downregulate type 1 helper T cell-mediated cellular immunity while upregulating type 2 helper T cell humoral activity to maintain fetal tolerance. Because host defense against Mycobacterium tuberculosis depends predominantly on robust cellular immune responses, this immunological shift compromises mycobacterial containment, thereby facilitating reactivation of latent foci, accelerated disease progression, and hematogenous dissemination to extrapulmonary sites including the meninges. The clinical course of this case reflects broader epidemiological realities and diagnostic obstacles surrounding pregnancy-associated tuberculosis. Global surveillance data from the World Health Organization recorded approximately 10.7 million new tuberculosis cases and over 1.2 million deaths worldwide in 2024, with China contributing 6.5 percent of this total disease burden. Tuberculous meningitis accounts for approximately 6 percent of extrapulmonary tuberculosis cases and remains one of the most fatal forms of the disease. A referenced systematic review of pregnancy-related tuberculous meningitis documented maternal mortality rates of 23 percent and fetal or neonatal mortality rates of 30 percent, with 30 percent of surviving mothers suffering permanent neurological impairments. To resolve these complex therapeutic dilemmas, the medical center organized its care pathway into four distinct operational decision domains managed by a unified multidisciplinary team. Rather than relying on sequential consultations, specialists in respiratory medicine, obstetrics, hepatology, endocrinology, pharmacy, and critical care maintained direct collaborative decision-making. The first domain focused on non-pharmacological intracranial pressure reduction via lumbar cisternal drainage and tolerable initial anti-tuberculosis therapy; the second governed timely escalation to linezolid and moxifloxacin when high fever persisted; the third managed viral suppression and liver safety through tenofovir and serial biochemistry; and the fourth coordinated antenatal monitoring and planned delivery timing. This approach echoed management strategies documented in earlier reports of gestational central nervous system tuberculosis complicated by seizures, while uniquely addressing the therapeutic tensions of severe active hepatitis B co-infection and systemic organ involvement. The authors concluded that structured multidisciplinary collaboration is indispensable for achieving favorable maternal and infant survival in complex cases of disseminated tuberculosis. The report provides evidence that combined cerebrospinal fluid analysis, clinical examination, and chest computed tomography can guide definitive therapeutic escalation even when magnetic resonance imaging cannot be safely performed. Furthermore, the findings highlight socioeconomic and geographic dimensions of disease management, noting that remote pastoral populations face significant barriers to timely healthcare access that exacerbate diagnostic delays. Expanding multidisciplinary care frameworks into resource-constrained settings remains essential to close persistent evidence gaps in maternal infectious disease management. The favorable maternal and neonatal outcomes achieved in a resource-limited setting further confirm the practical value of this integrated protocol. Recommendations tailored to you Sign in or create an account to see articles, videos, and podcasts matched to your specialties. Sign in or sign up Christina M. Madison, PharmD, FCCP, AAHIVP, introduces data presented at the 33rd Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections on long-acting cabotegravir/rilpivirine in people with viremia and adherence challenges. Joseph Burkhart, PharmD, calls it huge news that dramatically expands the pool of candidates. Previously, long-acting injectables were started only in patients already suppressed, simply to maintain suppression. Now, patients with active viremia and nonadherence may become candidates. That shift could prevent disease progression and onward transmission. Dr Madison adds that some patients have achieved suppression for the first time since their diagnosis. Tram Nguyen, PharmD, then discusses doravirine/islatravir, approved by the FDA in April 2026. It is a first-in-class, tenofovir-free, 2-drug oral regimen. It was noninferior to bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide in virologically suppressed adults. She explains that the indication is for patients with suppression, not for treatment-naive individuals. Candidates should have no history of treatment failure and no resistance to doravirine. Renal function matters, and she notes that dosing depends on whether estimated glomerular filtration rate is above or below 30. Studies also showed minimal weight change. That makes the regimen appealing for patients concerned about weight gain on current therapy. Because the regimen contains no tenofovir, it offers no activity against hepatitis B virus (HBV). Dr Nguyen stresses that hepatitis B serology must be completed before switching. HBV-positive patients were also excluded from the pivotal trials. Pharmacists must therefore screen for coinfection before recommending any switch to a tenofovir-sparing regimen. On coverage, Dr Nguyen reports that her patients on the regimen have been well covered without prior authorizations. In "Implementing Novel HIV Therapies: Pharmacist Roles in Retail and Clinic," Spencer Durham, PharmD, FCCP, BCPS, BCIDP, will address how pharmacists can make sure novel therapies actually reach the patients who need them. content_title: Guest Commentary: What ending vaccine mandates means for our kids
content: A nurse loads a syringe with a vaccine against hepatitis at a free immunization clinic for students before the start of the school year, in Lynwood, California August, 27, 2013. Florida is considering ending vaccine requirements for hepatitis and three other diseases. Robyn Beck/AFP Photo via Getty Images By Katrine L Wallace PUBLISHED: November 14, 2026 at 5:30 AM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... The Florida Department of Health held a hearing in October on a proposal to remove four vaccine requirements for entry into school and childcare: Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib), chickenpox , pneumococcal and hepatitis B . Prior to these vaccines, there were millions of chickenpox cases and thousands of serious bacterial infections and preventable deaths among American children each year. Vaccination has dramatically reduced the toll of these diseases. Many parents today grew up during the transition to widespread vaccination for these diseases and may never have witnessed the severe complications these vaccines help prevent. Katrine L. Wallace is an assistant professor of epidemiology and biostatistics at the University of Illinois Chicago. (courtesy, Katrine L. Wallace) I am an epidemiologist who studies vaccine-preventable illnesses and health communication, and I worry that perhaps the luxury of forgetting about these diseases could end up giving rise to a generation of children who aren’t vaccinated against them. School vaccination requirements help communities establish herd immunity . That occurs when enough people are vaccinated to prevent a disease from easily spreading. When vaccination rates fall, infections can spread among susceptible children throughout the community. Florida’s proposal would not eliminate these four vaccines, nor would ending a mandate mean that every family would stop using them. However, it would weaken one of the policies designed to maintain high vaccination coverage. If fewer children are vaccinated as a result, the risks will extend beyond the families making that choice. The consequences could be devastating. Before Hib vaccines became widely used in the late 1980s, pediatricians sometimes faced a terrifying emergency: an infant with fever, lethargy and a stiff neck. The testing of cerebrospinal fluid would reveal bacterial meningitis caused by Hib, an infection that could kill a child or leave lasting neurological damage. Today, many doctors have never seen a single case. The bacterium has not disappeared, but widespread vaccination has made serious Hib disease in young children far less common. Before the vaccine, Hib was the leading cause of bacterial meningitis. In the early 1980s, there were 20,000 invasive Hib infections among American children under 5 years old, 12,000 of which were meningitis. Between 3% and 6% of those children died , and between 15% and 30% of survivors were left deaf or with brain damage. By the early 1990s, there were more than 4 million cases of chickenpox annually in the U.S. Of those infected, 10,500 to 13,500 were hospitalized, and 100 to 150 died. More than 90% of cases and about 70% of hospitalizations occurred in children, as did roughly half of the deaths. Children are contagious before the rash appears, and each case has an incubation period of up to three weeks . A single infection could spread through a school or daycare in waves for a month or more. Since vaccination began in 1995, deaths from chickenpox in people under 20 years old have been virtually eliminated . Before the introduction of the childhood vaccine against pneumococcal bacteria in 2000, pneumococcal disease caused about 17,000 invasive infections annually in American children under age 5, including about 700 cases of meningitis and 200 deaths. On top of that, pneumococcal disease caused approximately 5 million ear infections. Hepatitis B can spread from an infected mother to her baby during childbirth and through contact with infected blood. People with chronic hepatitis B may have no symptoms and may not know they are infected, allowing the virus to spread unknowingly within families and communities. Infected infants and young children also are often asymptomatic. Yet the consequences can be serious. Infants who become infected with hepatitis B have about a 90% chance of developing chronic hepatitis B, which over time can cause cirrhosis and liver cancer. Before the hepatitis B vaccine became available in the U.S. in 1982, an estimated 20,000 American children were infected each year. In 1991, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommended universal infant hepatitis B vaccination as part of a comprehensive strategy to prevent transmission. The CDC estimates that perinatal hepatitis B infections in the United States declined by 75% between 1987 and 2000. An entire generation of parents has been spared the experience of seeing a child with Hib meningitis, or young adults with liver problems from chronic hepatitis B. Nor have they had to deal with finding alternate childcare for a month because a chickenpox outbreak has shut down their child’s preschool. These are achievements of vaccination — and a reminder of what can be forgotten when prevention works. Katrine L. Wallace is an assistant professor of epidemiology and biostatistics at the University of Illinois Chicago. This article is republished from The Conversation under a Creative Commons license. content: Bepirovirsen Market Size, Share, Trends and Forecast 2026-2035s The global Bepirovirsen Market is entering a significant growth phase as pharmaceutical companies, healthcare providers and investors increasingly focus on innovative treatments for chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Bepirovirsen, marketed under the brand name Hibsago by GSK, represents an important development in the treatment landscape because of its antisense oligonucleotide mechanism and potential to achieve a functional cure in eligible patients. Growing interest in finite-duration treatment approaches, improvements in hepatitis B diagnosis and regulatory progress are creating new commercial opportunities for this emerging pharmaceutical market. According to Ameco Research, the global Bepirovirsen Market was estimated at USD 35.2 million in 2026 and is projected to reach USD 1,986.5 million by 2035, registering a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 29.0% from 2027 to 2035. The market is expected to reach USD 258.4 million in 2027, representing its first full year of commercial sales. Get Sample Pages of this Premium Report: https://www.amecoresearch.com/sample/277168 The anticipated expansion reflects increasing commercial interest in antisense oligonucleotide therapeutics, growing demand for advanced chronic hepatitis B treatments, and the potential expansion of Bepirovirsen availability across major pharmaceutical markets. What Is the Bepirovirsen Market? The Bepirovirsen Market encompasses the development, commercialization, distribution and utilization of Bepirovirsen for treating chronic hepatitis B. Bepirovirsen, also identified as GSK3228836, is an antisense oligonucleotide originally discovered by Ionis Pharmaceuticals and developed in collaboration with GSK. The treatment is designed to target hepatitis B virus (HBV) RNA and reduce the production of viral proteins, including hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg). Reducing these viral proteins may help restore the immune system's ability to control the infection. Conventional nucleos(t)ide analogue treatments primarily suppress viral replication and generally require long-term administration. Bepirovirsen introduces a different therapeutic approach by targeting viral RNA and pursuing functional cure outcomes in eligible patients. A functional cure generally refers to sustained loss of detectable HBsAg alongside suppressed HBV DNA after treatment discontinuation. This distinction is commercially important because it introduces the possibility of a finite treatment course rather than indefinite viral suppression. Bepirovirsen Market Size and Forecast 2026-2035 The Bepirovirsen Market is projected to experience substantial expansion throughout the forecast period, supported by increasing commercialization and the potential adoption of innovative hepatitis B therapies. Ameco Research estimates that the market will increase from USD 35.2 million in 2026 to USD 1,986.5 million by 2035, representing a CAGR of 29.0% from 2027 to 2035. The first full year of commercial sales is expected to generate USD 258.4 million in 2027. Thereafter, the market is forecast to expand as treatment availability improves, additional patients are identified and healthcare systems establish appropriate treatment and reimbursement pathways. Key Bepirovirsen Market Statistics Market Indicator Market Value Market size, 2026 USD 35.2 million Market size, 2027 USD 258.4 million Market forecast, 2035 USD 1,986.5 million CAGR, 2027-2035 29.0% Base year 2026 Forecast period 2026-2035 The projected growth highlights the emerging commercial significance of Bepirovirsen within the global pharmaceutical industry. However, the realization of these forecasts will depend on patient eligibility, regulatory access, physician adoption, treatment affordability and reimbursement conditions. Key Factors Driving Bepirovirsen Market Growth Increasing Demand for Functional Cure Treatments for Hepatitis B One of the most important drivers of the Bepirovirsen Market is the unmet medical need associated with chronic hepatitis B. Existing antiviral treatments can effectively suppress viral replication, but sustained elimination of hepatitis B surface antigen remains difficult to achieve. Bepirovirsen offers a differentiated treatment approach by targeting viral RNA and reducing the production of hepatitis B viral proteins. Its potential to achieve functional cure in a proportion of eligible patients is increasing interest among pharmaceutical companies, healthcare professionals and patients. This shift toward functional cure-oriented treatment strategies is expected to support the commercial development of Bepirovirsen. Advancements in Antisense Oligonucleotide Technology Progress in antisense oligonucleotide technology is creating new opportunities for pharmaceutical innovation. These therapeutics are designed to interact with specific RNA sequences and influence protein production. Bepirovirsen demonstrates the potential application of RNA-targeting technology in chronic infectious diseases. Its development is also drawing attention to the broader potential of oligonucleotide-based medicines in addressing diseases where conventional therapies have important limitations. Continued investment in RNA-based therapeutics, improved drug delivery and clinical research is expected to support the long-term development of this market. Regulatory Approvals and Commercialization Opportunities Regulatory progress represents another important factor influencing Bepirovirsen Market growth. The Japanese approval in August 2026 and U.S. FDA approval in October 2026 represent significant milestones in its commercialization. These developments are expected to strengthen market access opportunities and encourage healthcare providers to evaluate the treatment for eligible patients. Future expansion will depend on regulatory decisions in additional countries, national reimbursement policies and the development of appropriate clinical treatment pathways. Growing Investment in Innovative Pharmaceutical Treatments Pharmaceutical companies are increasingly evaluating innovative therapeutic approaches that address substantial unmet medical needs. The development of functional cure treatments for hepatitis B is attracting attention because of the potential to transform long-term disease management. Strategic partnerships, research investments and commercialization agreements are expected to influence the competitive environment and accelerate the availability of innovative hepatitis B treatments. Bepirovirsen Market Segmentation Analysis The Bepirovirsen Market is segmented by baseline HBsAg level, HBeAg status, end user and distribution channel. These categories provide an understanding of patient eligibility, treatment demand and the commercial channels through which the therapy reaches healthcare providers and patients. By Baseline HBsAg Level Based on baseline hepatitis B surface antigen levels, the market is divided into: • ≤100 IU/mL • 100 to ≤1,000 IU/mL • 1,000 to ≤3,000 IU/mL The >100 to ≤1,000 IU/mL segment accounted for the largest market share of 38.9% in 2027. It is projected to maintain its leading position, reaching 39.6% by 2035. The >1,000 to ≤3,000 IU/mL category is expected to register the fastest growth, with a CAGR of approximately 31.6%. Its increasing contribution reflects the potential expansion of treatment adoption across eligible patient categories. By HBeAg Status The market is categorized into: • HBeAg-negative • HBeAg-positive HBeAg-negative patients represented the dominant segment, accounting for 83.2% of the market in 2027. This segment is projected to maintain its leadership, supported by its substantial representation within the treated chronic hepatitis B population. Meanwhile, the HBeAg-positive segment is expected to grow at a faster rate of approximately 30.7%, compared with 28.7% for the HBeAg-negative segment. By End User Based on end users, the Bepirovirsen Market is classified into: • Hospital hepatology and gastroenterology centers • Specialty clinics • Community health centers and others Hospital hepatology and gastroenterology centers dominated the market with a 57.1% share in 2027. Their leading position is associated with specialist expertise, patient assessment, treatment initiation and clinical monitoring requirements. Specialty clinics represent another important distribution and treatment setting. Community health centers and other facilities are expected to record the fastest growth, with a projected CAGR of approximately 35.1%. Increasing diagnostic accessibility and the expansion of treatment services beyond large hospitals could support this segment over the forecast period. By Distribution Channel The distribution channel segmentation includes: • Specialty pharmacies • Hospital pharmacies • Retail and online pharmacies Specialty pharmacies accounted for the largest distribution channel share at 47.3% in 2027. Their importance reflects the specialized handling, prescription coordination and patient support associated with advanced pharmaceutical treatments. The specialty pharmacy segment is projected to reach 51.6% of the market by 2035. Meanwhile, retail and online pharmacies are expected to register the fastest growth, supported by the potential expansion of outpatient treatment and self-administration practices. Regional Analysis of the Bepirovirsen Market Geographical commercialization, regulatory approvals and healthcare infrastructure will play important roles in determining the future development of the Bepirovirsen Market. North America North America is expected to remain the largest regional market, accounting for approximately 72.9% of global revenue in 2027. The region's leading position is supported by U.S. regulatory approval, established pharmaceutical distribution infrastructure and the availability of specialist healthcare services. However, its market share is projected to decline to approximately 46.9% by 2035 as commercialization expands into other regions. Europe Europe represents a significant emerging opportunity and is projected to be the fastest-growing regional market, registering a CAGR of approximately 50.7% from 2027 to 2035. Regulatory authorization, country-level reimbursement decisions and increasing access to specialist hepatitis B treatment are expected to influence regional adoption. The potential expansion of treatment availability across major European pharmaceutical markets could substantially strengthen the region's contribution to global revenue. Asia-Pacific Asia-Pacific represents an important long-term opportunity because of the substantial chronic hepatitis B patient population across several countries. Japan has already achieved an important regulatory milestone through its 2026 approval. China also represents a strategically important market because of its substantial patient population and evolving regulatory environment. The development of commercialization partnerships, improvements in diagnosis and the availability of affordable treatment options will influence the region's long-term growth. Latin America and Middle East & Africa Latin America and the Middle East & Africa represent additional opportunities for future market expansion. The development of healthcare infrastructure, improved hepatitis B screening, regulatory approvals and reimbursement arrangements will influence the pace of commercialization across these markets. Challenges and Restraints Affecting Bepirovirsen Market Expansion Despite its promising commercial outlook, the Bepirovirsen Market faces several challenges. Treatment eligibility limitations: Not every patient with chronic hepatitis B is eligible for Bepirovirsen treatment. Baseline HBsAg levels, clinical characteristics and existing treatment status influence patient selection. Pricing and reimbursement barriers: The cost of innovative pharmaceutical treatments can influence accessibility, particularly in countries with limited healthcare budgets and complex reimbursement systems. Clinical response variability: Functional cure outcomes are not achieved by every treated patient. Differences in baseline viral markers and individual patient characteristics may influence treatment response. Diagnostic limitations: Identifying eligible patients requires appropriate testing and clinical assessment. Inadequate access to diagnostic infrastructure could restrict the potential treatment population. Competitive therapeutic developments: Other investigational approaches, including RNA interference therapies, capsid assembly modulators and therapeutic vaccines, could influence the future competitive environment. Competitive Landscape of the Bepirovirsen Market The competitive environment includes pharmaceutical companies developing innovative hepatitis B treatments and technologies targeting viral replication and protein production. Key companies associated with the Bepirovirsen and broader chronic hepatitis B therapeutic landscape include: • GSK plc • Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc. • Sino Biopharmaceutical (Chia Tai Tianqing) • Gilead Sciences • Aligos Therapeutics • Arbutus Biopharma • Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals • Vir Biotechnology GSK plays the central commercial role in the Bepirovirsen market, while Ionis Pharmaceuticals contributed to the discovery and development of the drug. Sino Biopharmaceutical's partnership with GSK also represents an important development for potential commercialization in China. Competition from alternative therapeutic approaches is expected to encourage continued innovation, clinical research and strategic collaborations throughout the forecast period. Future Trends and Opportunities in the Bepirovirsen Market Several emerging trends are expected to shape the market through 2035. First, the transition from long-term viral suppression toward functional cure-oriented treatment strategies could influence pharmaceutical investment and treatment preferences. Second, improved hepatitis B screening and quantitative HBsAg testing could help identify patients who meet treatment eligibility requirements. Third, the expansion of regulatory approvals and commercialization partnerships is expected to create additional regional revenue opportunities. Fourth, continued development of antisense oligonucleotide technologies and combination treatment approaches could strengthen the broader therapeutic landscape. Finally, the expansion of specialty pharmaceutical distribution networks and patient support services may improve treatment accessibility and contribute to commercial adoption. content_title: Simplified GADA Model Improves HBV-Related Liver Cancer Detection in 23,098 Patients
content: Mirage News Mirage News Mirage News Science 20 Nov 2026 2:37 am AEDT Date Time Chinese Medical Journals Publishing House Co., Ltd. BEIJING, CHINA—Researchers from Peking University and collaborating hospitals across China have developed and validated GADA, a simplified model for detecting hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Derived from the established GALAD framework, GADA combines gender, age, des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin (DCP; also known as PIVKA-II), and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP). In more than 23,000 participants, it showed strong diagnostic performance for both overall and early-stage HCC. The study is forthcoming in the Chinese Medical Journal. Chronic HBV infection causes more than 40% of HCC cases worldwide and is associated with approximately 86% of HCC cases in China. The epidemiology of HCC in China therefore differs substantially from that in many Western cohorts, where hepatitis C, alcohol-related liver disease, and metabolic liver disease contribute more prominently. The GALAD model integrates gender, age, AFP, AFP-L3%, and DCP and has performed well in several Western populations. However, its performance required reassessment in HBV-associated chronic liver disease. AFP-L3% also adds measurement complexity, cost, and sample-volume requirements, and is not readily available in all clinical settings. The study, led by Professor Fengmin Lu was published online on August 17, 2026, in the Chinese Medical Journal . The investigators analyzed 2,190 adults with HBV-related chronic liver disease at Mengchao Hepatobiliary Hospital of Fujian Medical University. Participants were randomly assigned to a modeling cohort (70%; n = 1,533) and an internal validation cohort (30%; n = 657). A separate prospective external validation cohort enrolled 20,908 participants at ten hospitals across China, including 905 patients with newly diagnosed HCC and 20,003 patients without HCC (17,802 with chronic hepatitis B and 2,201 with HBV-related cirrhosis). Altogether, 23,098 participants were included. AFP and DCP provided complementary diagnostic information, whereas AFP-L3% contributed limited additional utility in this HBV-focused population. The researchers therefore developed the four-variable GADA score: Z = –11.111 + 1.122 x gender + 0.073 x age + 2.660 x log10(DCP) + 0.578 x log10(AFP) Gender is coded as 1 for male and 0 for female. Cohort AUC (95% CI) Sensitivity Specificity Modeling 0.940 (0.927–0.952) 82.57% 91.53% Internal validation 0.935 (0.914–0.953) 82.04% 92.65% External validation 0.919 (0.916–0.923) 86.00% 81.88% In the modeling cohort, GADA outperformed the original GALAD model (AUC 0.940 vs. 0.907). In the external validation cohort, it also outperformed AFP alone (AUC 0.748) and DCP alone (AUC 0.841). Center-specific AUCs ranged from 0.895 to 0.977, supporting robustness across geographically and clinically diverse settings. For early-stage HCC meeting the Milan criteria, GADA achieved AUCs of 0.858 in the modeling cohort, 0.868 in the internal validation cohort, and 0.903 in the external validation cohort. In the external cohort, sensitivity was 88.16% and specificity was 74.50%. GADA was designed for the setting in which the clinical need is greatest in China: distinguishing HBV-related HCC from chronic hepatitis B and HBV-related cirrhosis. By removing AFP-L3% while preserving strong diagnostic accuracy, the model may reduce testing complexity and improve accessibility, including in hospitals with more limited laboratory resources. The model should be viewed as an adjunct to established HCC surveillance and diagnostic pathways, not as a replacement for imaging or clinical assessment. Prospective evaluation in routine surveillance populations and calibration of operational thresholds across laboratories will be important before broad implementation. DOI: 10.1097/CM9.0000000000004244 Prof. Fengmin Lu is Director of the Peking University Infectious Disease Research Center, Professor in the Department of Microbiology at Peking University Health Science Center, and a jointly appointed Professor at the Center for Infectious Diseases, Peking University Third Hospital. His research focuses on the molecular mechanisms of HBV-related hepatocarcinogenesis, occult HBV infection, and biomarkers. He led the development and multicenter validation of the GADA model. He has led more than 20 national research projects, received two Second-Class National Science and Technology Progress Awards, published nearly 200 papers, and holds 25 authorized invention patents, seven of which have been commercialized. This work was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (No. 82272433) and the Fujian Provincial Key Laboratory of Hepatic Drug Research (No. 2022-YF-0050). /Public Release. content: X 新闻 体育 汽车 房产 旅游 教育 时尚 科技 财经 娱乐 母婴 健康 历史 军事 美食 更多 文化 星座 专题 游戏 搞笑 动漫 宠物 新闻 体育 汽车 房产 旅游 教育 时尚 科技 财经 娱乐 母婴 健康 历史 军事 美食 文化 星座 专题 游戏 搞笑 动漫 宠物 更多 无障碍 关怀版 登录 脂肪肝通过诱导肝细胞凋亡助力乙肝病毒清除 2026-11-19 11:12 来源: 尔尔呀 链接复制成功 发布于:北京市 慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)合并代谢相关脂肪性肝病(MAFLD)的患病率不断升高,已有临床观察发现MAFLD的乙肝患者病毒复制水平更低,但具体机制尚不明确。该研究结合人体肝转录组与细胞实验,探究脂毒性诱导的肝细胞凋亡对乙肝病毒(HBV)的清除作用。 结果显示:CHB合并代谢相关脂肪性肝炎(MASH)患者肝脏凋亡相关基因上调,线粒体功能及氧化应激相关基因下调。体外研究显示棕榈酸(PA)通过线粒体损伤与氧化应激诱导肝细胞凋亡进而促进HBV清除。 然而,通过促进细胞凋亡来清除HBV可能并非完全有益。脂毒性诱导的肝细胞凋亡会加速肝损伤,进而可能推动MASH、肝纤维化/肝硬化甚至肝细胞癌的进展。有数据提示,CHB合并肝脂肪变性与乙肝表面抗原清除率提高三倍相关,但也会使肝纤维化进展的风险增加两倍。 参考文献: Yu JY, Zheng X. title: 专访浩博医药程国锋:从吉利德到浩博,攻坚乙肝功能性治愈
excerpt: 对于有限疗程治疗而言,停药后的持久性恰恰是衡量临床价值的重要维度。南方医科大学南方医院侯金林教授在接受《感染在线》采访时表示,AHB-137长期随访中达到完全应答并停用全部治疗的患者,持久应答率超过90%,这一结果为功能性治愈的长期维持提供了新的证据。
